action.addComponent: Adds a component to the entity with the given field values. Goes through the command buffer, so it lands at the end of the tick.
action.addModifier: Puts a modifier source into the entity source list under an id; the value is a multiplier in Q16.16.
action.addTween: Starts a tween on the entity: definition index, bounds, duration and easing.
action.carveFloor: Removes the arena floor around a world position; the radius is a distance in Q16.16, not a number of cells.
action.destroyEntity: Destroys the entity. Like every mutation, it is deferred to the end of the tick.
action.emitEvent: Emits an event of the given type with a map of data fields onto the bus of the current tick.
action.forEach: Runs the body for every entity of the query, binding the entity to a name. The result is materialized before the walk.
action.forEachEvent: Runs the body for every event of the given type on the bus of the current tick, binding a reference to the event.
action.if: Branching over a boolean condition: runs `then`, otherwise `else` when it is given.
action.let: Binds expression values to names and runs the body with them. Bindings are computed in the outer scope, not chained one after another.
action.modifyComponent: Writes values into fields of a component the entity already has.
action.random: Binds a random Q16.16 value of the system stream to a name and runs the body. An action, not an operator: advancing the generator is an effect.
action.randomBelow: Binds a uniform integer in [0, bound) of the system stream to a name and runs the body.
action.removeComponent: Removes the component from the entity.
action.removeModifier: Removes a modifier source by id; an absent id is not an error.
action.set: Assigns a new value to a mutable `let` binding: this is what turns `let` into an accumulator and `forEach` into a fold. The iteration variable of `as` is immutable.
action.spawnEntity: Spawns an entity from a prefab, optionally overriding component field values.
operation.document.list.append: Appends a record to the end of a tracked list and returns its session descriptor. Only to the end: the order of records fixes the ids the scene hands out.
operation.document.list.remove: Removes the record addressed by the descriptor. Indices of the records after it shift, and that is not a defect: the removed object really is gone.
operation.document.list.removeValue: Removes a place inside a record addressed by a descriptor. An empty path is refused: the record itself is removed by the record operation.
operation.document.list.setValue: Writes a value inside a record addressed by a descriptor; the path is counted from the record, not from the document root.
operation.document.removeValue: Removes the place at a path: the object key disappears rather than becoming null — those are different documents.
operation.document.renameKey: Renames an object key in place. A separate operation rather than a remove-and-write pair: editor document keys are never sorted, so a removed entry would move to the end of the object and turn one diff block into two. The path leads to the holding object, not to the key itself.
operation.document.setValue: Writes a value at a path in the document. The path must not lead into a tracked list: its records are addressed by descriptor.
operation.param.document: Identifier of an open document — its path from the root of the content tree.
operation.param.from: The former key name. If the object has no such key the operation refuses: there is nothing to rename.
operation.param.item: The record being appended: any JSON, up to a whole subtree.
operation.param.list: Path of the tracked list whose records are addressed by session descriptors.
operation.param.path: Path to a place in the document: a list of steps, where a string is an object key and a number is a list index.
operation.param.record: Session descriptor of a list record. It lives in the memory of the current session only; a reference kept between sessions is invalid.
operation.param.to: The new key name. A name already taken in this object is rejected — including a name equal to the former one.
operation.param.value: The value being written: any JSON, up to a whole subtree.
operator.!=: Inequality of two scalars; vectors are compared component-wise, not as a whole.
operator.==: Equality of two scalars; vectors are compared component-wise, not as a whole.
operator.and: True when every argument is true; two arguments at least.
operator.bitTest: Tests bit 0..31 of an `i32` mask — the only bit operation of the language.
operator.clamp: Clamps a value to the [min, max] range.
operator.cos: Cosine; the angle is a Q16.16 fraction of a turn, 16384 is a quarter.
operator.eventField: Data field of the event bound by forEachEvent; the scale is not converted, the emitter knows it.
operator.fromInt: Converts a raw `i32` value to Q16.16.
operator.getComponent: Value of a component field of the entity.
operator.hasComponent: Whether the entity has the component.
operator.hasFloorAt: Whether there is floor under a world position; a scene without terrain is an error, not false.
operator.if: Pure branching `[cond, then, …, else]`; expressions have no loops.
operator.or: True when at least one argument is true; two arguments at least.
operator.raycastEntity: Entity of the nearest ray hit; a static collider and no hit alike answer -1 — `raycastHit` tells them apart.
operator.raycastHit: Whether the ray between two points meets a collider; a scene without the Physics API is an error, not a miss.
operator.raycastPoint: Point of the nearest ray hit; without a hit it is the far end of the segment.
operator.sin: Sine; the angle is a Q16.16 fraction of a turn, 16384 is a quarter.
operator.sqrt: Square root of a Q16.16 number.
operator.tick: Number of the current tick — a raw integer, arithmetic on it needs fromInt.
operator.toInt: Converts a Q16.16 value to a raw integer.
operator.var: Value of a local variable: a system argument or a `let` binding.
operator.vec: Builds a vector from two Q16.16 components.
operator.vec\\.lengthSq: Squared length of a vector: no square root, and exact.
operator.vec\\.normalize: Unit vector of the same direction.
operator.vec\\.scale: Vector scaled by a Q16.16 number.
schema.arena.radius: Starting arena radius in Q16.16; from there on the radius lives in a component.
schema.component.defaults: Default field values of the component; values of `fixed` fields are in Q16.16.
schema.component.fields: Fields of the component: name to type, `i32` or `fixed`.
schema.component.name: Component name: systems, prefabs and placement address it by this name.
schema.inputFrame.aimDir: Aim direction as a Q16.16 fraction of a turn.
schema.inputFrame.move: Movement vector of the frame in Q16.16.
schema.inputFrame.seq: Sequence number of the frame on the client.
schema.prefab.components: Components of the prefab and the initial values of their fields.
schema.prefab.name: Prefab name: placement refers to it.
schema.query.all: The entity must have every listed component.
schema.query.any: The entity must have at least one of the listed components.
schema.query.not: The entity must have none of the listed components.
schema.query.withTag: The entity must carry the tag.
schema.query.withinRadius: Narrows the query to a circle around a point.
schema.query.withinRadius.center: Center of the circle: an expression yielding a vector.
schema.query.withinRadius.radius: Radius of the circle: an expression in Q16.16.
schema.scenario.initial: Placement of the run: applied after the placement of the scene.
schema.scenario.inputs: Input frames of the run, one per player and tick.
schema.scenario.locomotion: Enables native locomotion in the run. A field of the scenario, not of the scene: which implementation moves the hero is a build dependency.
schema.scenario.locomotion.colliderCompo: Name of the collider component: the cliff rise of the jump is written into it for the duration of the jump.
schema.scenario.locomotion.configCompone: Name of the configuration component: every tunable number of movement is a field of it.
schema.scenario.locomotion.dodgeButton: Index of the dodge bit in the button mask; the engine does not know the input layout.
schema.scenario.locomotion.inputComponen: Name of the input component: its fields are written by the input system.
schema.scenario.locomotion.jumpButton: Index of the jump bit in the button mask; the engine does not know the input layout.
schema.scenario.locomotion.lockComponent: Name of the selective action lock component with the `mask` field: while the maneuver bit is set, dodge and jump do not start, and ordinary movement keeps working. Not set — the lock is not read at all.
schema.scenario.locomotion.maneuverLockB: Index of the «maneuvers forbidden» bit in the lock mask; the meaning of the other bits is a convention of the content. Requires the lock component.
schema.scenario.locomotion.name: Name of the locomotion system: the name of its RNG stream and the key it is substituted by.
schema.scenario.locomotion.stateComponen: Name of the maneuver state machine component: dodge, double-tap window, roll, airborne.
schema.scenario.locomotion.velocityCompo: Name of the velocity component the physics integrates.
schema.scenario.name: Scenario name; the baseline file is named after it.
schema.scenario.physics: Enables physics in the run. A field of the scenario, not of the scene: the implementation is a build dependency.
schema.scenario.players: Players of the run; the order defines the player slots.
schema.scenario.scene: Scene config the run starts from.
schema.scenario.seed: World seed; the RNG streams derive from it.
schema.scenario.visibility: Enables visibility recomputation in the run. A field of the scenario, not of the scene: the system needs raycast.
schema.scene.arena: Arena asset: the radius and border state components and their prefab are derived from it by the loader.
schema.scene.capacity: Upper bound on the number of entities in the world.
schema.scene.components: Component schemas of the scene; the order defines the component bit ids and is part of the format.
schema.scene.fog: Enables the fog of war components.
schema.scene.initial: Placement of the scene: what stands on the arena in every run of it. The order of entries is normative.
schema.scene.modifierSlots: Number of slots in modifier source lists; four by default.
schema.scene.terrain: Terrain asset: the floor map component and its prefab are derived from it by the loader.
schema.scene.timeScale: Enables the time scale and the merging of its modifier sources.
schema.scene.tweens: Table of tween definitions; a non-empty table enables the tween system.
schema.spawnEntry.overrides: Map of component to field to value on top of the prefab values.
schema.system.as: Name the entity of the query is bound to in the body of the system.
schema.system.do: Body of the system: actions executed in order.
schema.system.name: System name: the name of its RNG stream and the key a native system substitutes it by.
schema.system.order: Place of the system within the tick; equal orders are not allowed.
schema.system.query: Query over entities; sugar over the forEach action.
schema.terrain.flags: Cell flags, one string per row: `.` normal, `^` ramp, `_` no floor.
schema.terrain.levels: Level map, one string per row, one uppercase hexadecimal digit per cell.
schema.tweenDef.onComplete: Actions executed when the tween completes.
schema.tweenDef.target: Path to the component field the tween drives, for example `Health.value`.

validation.rule.assets.curvature: Checks a terrain curvature map with the assets validator: integer node offsets and node grid shape.
validation.rule.assets.manifest: Checks a visual manifest with the assets validator: entity records, models, textures, skins and animation names.
validation.rule.core.scene: Checks a scene config with the engine scene loader: component set, prefabs, systems, initial placement and arena assets — the same call the game client makes on load.
validation.rule.core.system: Checks a JSON system against every open scene: the engine resolves the component and prefab names the system refers to, then builds its body.
validation.rule.core.terrain: Checks a terrain asset with the engine grid builder: level and flag ranges, map alphabets and ramp width.
validation.rule.editor.cameraEffectState: Finds a lasting-effects table record in the manifest whose key matches no component of any open scene. A warning rather than an error: the manifest outlives the code, and the scene declaring that component may simply not be open (ASSET-8).
validation.rule.editor.curvatureGrid: Compares the curvature map grid with the terrain grid. A mismatch is a warning: at runtime the map is ignored rather than rejected (ASSET-7).
validation.rule.editor.decorationVisual: Finds a paired presentation document record whose `visual` does not resolve to a visual manifest record. A warning rather than an error: at runtime such a record is drawn as a placeholder and the rest of the scene draws as usual (ASSET-6).
validation.rule.editor.placementPrefab: Finds a placement record naming a prefab that no open scene declares; the record itself is addressed, not the scene as a whole (SER-8).
validation.rule.editor.prefabForVisual: Finds a visual manifest record that has no prefab behind it — the other half of the same pair (ED-19).
validation.rule.editor.visualForPrefab: Finds a prefab that has no visual manifest record: the author edits a unit as one entity, and the pair behind it must not drift apart (ED-19).
validation.rule.save.group.writeTogether: Requires the edits of one document group to reach disk in a single write; the rule judges the save itself, not the state of the tree (ED-21).
